title: OpenCode HTTP Minimal Session Canary
summary: The FP-MCP-246 minimal OpenCode HTTP session lifecycle canary ran successfully with cleanup enabled. It created one titled OpenCode session, observed /session/status before and after creation, read /session/{sessionID}, deleted only the created canary session, and observed /session/status after deletion. The canary returned sessionCreated=true, sessionDeleted=true, createHttpStatus=200, detailHttpStatus=200, deleteHttpStatus=200. It also confirmed promptSubmitted=false, messageEndpointCalled=false, waitEndpointCalled=false, runnerStartEndpointContacted=false, and opencodeStarted=false. The created session detail shape exposed top-level keys: cost, directory, id, path, projectID, slug, time, title, tokens, version. A key observation is that /session/status remained an empty object throughout: beforeSessionLikeEntryCount=0, afterCreateSessionLikeEntryCount=0, afterDeleteSessionLikeEntryCount=0, and sessionIdPresentAfterCreate=false. This suggests /session/status does not list idle/newly-created sessions and should not be treated as the only session-existence source.
caveats: The canary mutated OpenCode session state by creating and then deleting one canary session; it did not mutate ForgePilot execution state.
The session id was visible from POST /session and GET /session/{sessionID}, but it was not visible in /session/status after creation.

The empty /session/status map after session creation means status likely tracks active/busy session execution state rather than all sessions; this requires further verification before using it as a completion source.
No OpenCode prompt was submitted and no model call occurred.
boundaries: No OpenCode message endpoint was called.
No OpenCode wait endpoint was called.
No ForgePilot runner start endpoint was contacted.
No OpenCode process was started by this canary.
No execution approval was created, consumed, or authorized.
No local execution clearance was created.
Only the canary-created session was deleted.
